source.text:
### Problem

.internal is officially revered by [ICANN](https://www.icann.org/en/board-activities-and-meetings/materials/approved-resolutions-special-meeting-of-the-icann-board-29-07-2024-en#section2.a) and [IETF](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/draft-davies-internal-tld/) for private use. Please consider allow *.internal wildcard TLS certificates.

context.scope: Bounded candidate change to curl certificate allowance for the literal wildcard identity *.internal; not a standalone TLS specification or approved implementation contract. Externally authored, procedurally selected material, not blinded/held-out.

domains.title: Allow *.internal wildcard TLS certificate
domains.input_surface: TLS connection attempt, destination hostname, presented certificate and existing verification configuration
domains.observation_surface: certificate allowance or verification rejection attributable to the requested wildcard identity
domains.inherited_context: The surrounding curl application is the change target. No precise hostname matching, trust, identity-field or backend policy is imported from memory or implementation.

obligations.source_quote: Please consider allow *.internal wildcard TLS certificates.

parameters.domain: curl TLS certificate verification involving the literal wildcard identity *.internal
parameters.condition: The requested feature is adopted in an authorized scope; other applicable verification conditions are satisfied
parameters.observable: allowance of the requested wildcard certificate identity
parameters.required_change: *.internal is not categorically disallowed as a wildcard certificate identity
parameters.frame: No whole-application preservation guarantee or new TLS trust/hostname policy is asserted

obligations.statement: Allow *.internal wildcard TLS certificates as a bounded curl software change. This is not a requirement to accept every certificate carrying that identity irrespective of other verification conditions.

parameters.condition: An otherwise admissible TLS verification scenario in the authorized change scope
parameters.forbidden_reason: Categorical exclusion solely because the wildcard identity is *.internal
parameters.frame: Other verification conditions are not resolved or disabled by this obligation

obligations.statement: An otherwise admissible certificate must not be rejected solely because its wildcard identity is *.internal. Denying all such identities would deny A02-E1. No concrete hostname, trust fixture or success code is invented.

issues.description: Required independent/source-owner or appointed benchmark-owner approval of this exact bounded-change interpretation is unavailable. Confirm the adopted scope and authorized inherited verification context before sealing a complete FRC. This is an authority boundary, not a demonstrated material behavioral contradiction in the source.
alternatives: Approve the exact bounded-change candidate with identified inherited context
Supply an authorized different scope/context in a separately linked record

unspecified: No existing behavior is explicitly required by the source to remain unchanged; no universal preservation obligation is invented.

Hostname examples, SAN/common-name treatment and concrete inherited trust/expiry validation rules are not supplied. This change request need not restate them; any later oracle needs legitimate contextual authority rather than conventional curl behavior assumed from memory.
Exact error text/code, HTTP payload, TLS version, target curl version and backend enumeration are not source requirements. Their omission alone does not demonstrate material ambiguity.
No durable-state effects, migration, audit or restart behavior is specified; silence does not imply an effect prohibition.
No explicit choice of default/option activation or broad matching expansion is delegated. The candidate does not select a new flag, disable verification, admit nested/apex names or alter other TLDs.
The ICANN/IETF links supply attributed rationale only; their contents were not opened or accepted as new normative authority.
implementation_choices: Internal algorithm, data representation, helper organization and implementation strategy may vary provided the approved observable change is met; no source-required internal design exists.
Verification fixtures and internal test organization may vary after expectations are independently authorized; fixture selection cannot redefine required hostname or trust behavior.
No permission to choose new observable TLS matching/trust/activation policy is inferred from unspecified implementation details.
